title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Power
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: Federal alert sharpens: Iran-affiliated hackers are actively manipulating the PLCs that run US energy infrastructure
items.content_text: Federal agencies sharpened their warning that Iran-affiliated hackers are actively manipulating the programmable logic controllers that run US energy infrastructure. The joint advisory AA26-097A, updated 22 July, confirms actors have reached internet-exposed Rockwell, Schneider Electric and Siemens controllers, stolen project files, and rewritten or deleted control logic — in some cases disabling the shutdown and alarm functions that keep equipment inside safe limits, without alerting operators. For grid and generation operators the concern is direct: the same brands sit in substations, plants and remote sites, and a controller that suppresses its own alarms undermines the protection logic crews rely on. The campaign has already caused operational disruption and financial loss across the energy sector. It is not sophisticated — it targets devices left reachable from the internet with weak credentials.

items.title: FSB Center 16 router campaign (AA26-194A): the exposed edge gear sitting in front of substation networks
items.content_text: A joint advisory from NSA, CISA, the FBI and roughly a dozen partner nations (AA26-194A, 13 July) details how Russia’s FSB Center 16 — tracked as Static Tundra, Berserk Bear, Energetic Bear and Dragonfly — scans for network devices exposing SNMP with default community strings and abuses Cisco Smart Install to copy device configurations. Energy and state/local government are named explicitly. The same internet-facing edge routers, often with SNMP left open, sit directly in front of substation SCADA and control-center networks, and a stolen config is a ready-made map of the network before an intruder touches a relay or RTU.

items.title: FortiSandbox RCE flaws added to CISA KEV — exploited edge appliances on the utility IT/OT boundary
items.content_text: CISA added two critical Fortinet vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-39808 and CVE-2026-25089 (both CVSS 9.1), to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 16 July after evidence of exploitation in the wild. The flaws are OS command-injection bugs in FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud and PaaS that let an unauthenticated attacker run commands via crafted HTTP requests. Fortinet appliances routinely sit on the security boundary between utility IT and OT; a compromised inspection appliance is both a foothold and a blind spot. CISA set a 19 July federal remediation deadline.

items.title: Solar and storage inverters flagged as a remote-sabotage path as the grid leans on DER
items.content_text: Renewed research and industry attention this month centers on the cyber exposure of grid-connected solar inverters and battery storage as distributed energy resources become a larger share of generation. Analysts warn that inverters and their cloud-management platforms can be remotely manipulated — plaintext control channels, predictable session handling and internet-exposed management have all surfaced in recent DER advisories — and that coordinated manipulation of enough inverter capacity could stress grid stability. For utilities integrating third-party DER, the takeaway is that inverter fleets are OT assets that need the same segmentation, monitoring and vendor-security scrutiny as any control system.

items.title: Schneider Easergy MiCOM Px40 relays: hard-coded SNMP credentials expose device information (CVE-2026-4832)
items.content_text: CISA published ICSA-26-190-03 on 9 July covering CVE-2026-4832 in Schneider Electric’s Easergy MiCOM Px40 protection-relay series. The issue is a use of hard-coded credentials in the relay’s SNMP interface (CVSS v3 base score 5.3): an unauthenticated attacker able to reach the SNMP port can query and expose basic device identification information. It is an information-exposure weakness, not remote code execution — but protection relays are high-consequence substation assets and shouldn’t be exposing SNMP to untrusted networks in the first place. No public exploitation is known; treat this as patch-and-harden.

items.title: Hitachi Energy e-mesh EMS: unauthenticated heap-overflow (CVE-2026-42945, CVSS 9.2) in a utility energy-management platform
items.content_text: CISA and Hitachi Energy disclosed CVE-2026-42945 in the e-mesh energy management system (advisory ICSA-26-188-03, published 7 July). It is a heap-based buffer overflow in the NGINX web-server component bundled with the product, triggerable by an unauthenticated, remote attacker via a crafted HTTP request; it carries a CVSS v3.1 base score of 8.1 and a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2. e-mesh EMS is used to manage energy-storage and DER assets, so a compromised instance is both an operational-data exposure and a foothold inside the utility environment. No public exploitation is reported yet, but the unauthenticated, network-reachable nature makes patching a priority. A companion advisory the same day covered Hitachi Energy PROMOD V.

items.title: FERC-approved CIP virtualization standards and INSM monitoring set the grid’s compliance runway
items.content_text: FERC Order 919 approved an updated set of CIP standards (CIP-002-7 through CIP-013-3) covering virtualized environments, effective 26 May 2026 with mandatory compliance by 1 July 2028. Separately, CIP-015-1 (Order 907) requires Internal Network Security Monitoring for applicable control centers by 2 September 2028 and other entities by 2 September 2030. Nothing changes operationally today, but planning for INSM and virtualization compliance — visibility inside the electronic security perimeter — is work that starts now.

items.title: SEIA publishes cybersecurity priorities for the US solar and storage industry
items.content_text: The Solar Energy Industries Association released a report this month, “Cybersecurity Priorities for America’s Solar & Storage Industry,” setting out measures to harden inverter technology — supply-chain traceability, national inverter-cybersecurity guidance, and shared resources across the industry. It is guidance, not a mandate, but it signals where DER security expectations are heading and gives utilities and developers a reference as inverter fleets grow.
